Like-for-Like Quotes on Managed B200, B300, and NVL72 Capacity

# Which GPU Providers Give Like-for-Like Quotes on Managed B200, B300, and NVL72 Capacity?

September 25, 2026

Shortlist the providers that will answer one written request for quote (RFQ) line by line: a per-GPU-hour rate at a GPU count you set, managed scope itemized service by service, storage and networking priced on their own lines, and the term, delivery date, and support spelled out. However low it looks, a single node-hour or rack figure with no itemized scope can't be compared fairly until the provider fills in the GPU count, billing unit, term, and what the rate includes.

For managed HGX B200 and B300 clusters, send the RFQ to Together AI and Nebius, which both publicly list HGX B300 alongside managed Kubernetes, and to AWS for P6-B200 and P6-B300, where the managed layer has to be confirmed separately. For NVL72, include CoreWeave, Together AI, and Nebius, which quotes NVL72 on request. Put GMI Cloud on the list as well: GMI prices GPUs per GPU-hour, with networking and storage provisioned separately based on the workload, and all NVIDIA Blackwell hardware on GMI Cloud is currently in pre-order. Our managed clusters list H200 and B200 node types today. GB200 NVL72 and GB300 NVL72 are pre-order GPU platforms, and whether an NVL72 reservation includes a managed layer, and how far it goes, is set in the pre-order quote rather than in the current cluster catalog. B300 is a hardware option on Prime Inference, our dedicated inference service, and like the rest of our Blackwell lineup it is in pre-order. The comparison only holds once every quote uses the same unit, GPU count, and scope.

## Why managed Blackwell quotes don't line up

Managed Blackwell quotes usually differ in five ways before price even comes into it:

- Pricing unit. One provider quotes per GPU-hour, another per 8-GPU node-hour, and a third per rack or per multi-GPU instance.
- What "managed" covers. Some rates include the Kubernetes control plane, monitoring, and hardware replacement. Others price the managed layer as a separate fee or leave parts of it to you.
- Minimum allocation. HGX B200 and B300 come in 8-GPU nodes. NVL72 systems are built as 72-GPU racks, and some providers only sell them as full racks.
- Term. Weeks, months, or years, prepaid or billed monthly, with discounts that depend on all of these.
- Extra line items. Storage, egress, IP addresses, and support tiers are included by some providers and billed separately by others.

The RFQ below forces every provider to answer those five points in the same format.

## Send every provider the same RFQ

Send the same text to every provider and ask for answers in the same order. A blank field is recorded as "not quoted," not as zero.

```text
RFQ: managed Blackwell capacity

1. Systems and counts
   - HGX B200: 72 GPUs (9 nodes) and 144 GPUs (18 nodes)
   - HGX B300: 72 GPUs (9 nodes) and 144 GPUs (18 nodes)
   - NVL72 (GB200 or GB300): 1 rack (72 GPUs) and 2 racks (144 GPUs)
2. Price
   - Rate per GPU-hour for each system and count
   - The unit you actually bill in (GPU, node, instance, rack) and GPUs per unit
   - Minimum allocation and whether partial racks are sold
3. Managed scope (included / separate fee / not offered, per line)
   - Kubernetes control plane and version upgrades
   - GPU drivers, CUDA, and NCCL images
   - Scheduler (Kubernetes, Slurm, or both)
   - Monitoring and alerting
   - Hardware failure detection and replacement
   - NVL72 only: rack-scale NVLink fabric management, IMEX, Arm64 node images
4. Storage and networking, priced separately
   - Shared file system, object storage, local NVMe
   - Egress, ingress, public IPs, high-speed interconnect
5. Term and commitment
   - Term lengths offered, prepaid vs. monthly, discount per term
   - Price for added nodes or racks during the term
6. Delivery
   - Delivery date or window, and what happens if it slips
   - Current status of each system (available now or pre-order)
7. Support
   - Response times, named contacts, and whether support is in the rate
8. Region or data center for each system

```

The GPU counts are chosen on purpose. Seventy-two GPUs is exactly nine 8-GPU nodes and exactly one NVL72 rack, so a provider can quote the same GPU count across all three systems. Quoting two sizes also shows whether the per-GPU rate steps down with scale. Some providers list minimum cluster sizes above 144 GPUs: Together AI's GPU Clusters page, for example, lists HGX B200 clusters from 256 GPUs and GB200 NVL72 clusters from 512 GPUs. Ask those providers to quote at their minimum size as well, and record that minimum in the "minimum billable GPU count" column.

## Normalize to GPU-hours at the same GPU count

Convert every price to one unit before comparing:

Rate per GPU-hour = price per billing unit per hour ÷ GPUs in that unit

A node-hour price for HGX B200 or B300 divides by eight, since NVIDIA's HGX platform is a single baseboard with eight Blackwell or Blackwell Ultra GPUs. A rack price divides by 72. Providers that split NVL72 into smaller instances need one more step: CoreWeave's documentation describes its GB200 instances as four GPUs per node and requires NVL72 instances to be deployed as full racks of 18 nodes, so a per-node figure divides by four and the minimum purchase is still 72 GPUs.

Then check the count behind the rate. Lambda's 1-Click Clusters page, for example, publishes per-GPU-hour rates for HGX B200 that step down at 16, 64, and 256 or more GPUs. A per-GPU rate is only comparable with another rate quoted at the same GPU count and term.

Minimum allocation changes the real bill. A team that needs 64 GPUs pays for eight HGX nodes, but on a provider that sells NVL72 only as full racks, the NVL72 option costs 72 GPUs' worth of hours. Put the minimum billable GPU count next to each rate and multiply by that, not by the count you need.
